objective: Prove that if the triple system of gr n is nonabelian then counting maps from 2-surgeries on knots into N x| C2 is #P-hard, as far as the gadget calculus extends (class at most 4), by one-parameter-subgroup bases, the general steering lemma, the B-twisted edge weight and Bulatov-Grohe; combine with ticket A into the r = 2 dichotomy and state the gaps (class at least 5, non-graded algebras).
status: Proved by TRIPLE-SYSTEM-20261027-001C-P001: for p >= 5 and graded nilpotent Lie algebras of class at most 4 with a graded involution, a nonabelian Lie triple system ([[n-, n-], n-] != 0) makes counting maps from 2-surgeries on knots into N x| C2 #P-hard. The tools are one-parameter-subgroup bases, steering by the degree-3 Lie part of cable conjugators on all free minus classes (every class-4 correction has the trivial character; experiment B supported), the gadget, an integer even edge weight with 0 < f(0, s*) < f(0) whenever B != 0, and Bulatov-Grohe on f^2. With ticket A this gives the r = 2 dichotomy: polynomial iff the triple system is abelian.
title: A nonabelian triple system makes counting #P-hard: the r = 2 dichotomy
